title: Abba Joseph's ten lamps
hook: Abba Joseph lifts his hands, his fingers like ten lamps: why not become all flame?
carry: not a longer list: the whole self, given
tomorrow: a hunter finds Antony laughing with his monks. why?

segments.voice: Abba Moses walked into a judgment with sand pouring out of a basket behind him, and the judging stopped. Your line: my own sins trail behind. A new week starts with an elder's hands.
screen: `MY OWN SINS TRAIL BEHIND.` → `A NEW WEEK IN THE DESERT.`

segments.voice: A habit tracker shows a perfect week. Every box checked, a little flame for the streak. And still the thought comes: what else should I add? A monk named Lot carries that exact question across the desert to an older monk, Abba Joseph. As far as I can, he says, I keep my little round of prayers. I fast a little. I pray, I think on scripture, I live at peace with others, and as far as I can, I keep my thoughts clean. So what else should I do? Joseph doesn't answer right away. He gets up.
screen: `EVERY BOX CHECKED.` → `WHAT ELSE SHOULD I ADD?` → `ABBA JOSEPH GETS UP.`

segments.voice: He doesn't add an item. He stretches his hands toward heaven, and the saying tells us his fingers became like ten lamps of fire. Then the answer: if you will, you can become all flame. That's the whole reply. Look at what it does to Lot's list. Nothing on it is wrong, and Joseph throws none of it out. But Lot measures in littles: as far as I can, a little. Joseph answers with all. Not more tasks. The same prayers, the same peace, with the whole person caught up in them. And he answers with his body first. The first letter to Timothy already pictures prayer that way: "I will therefore that men pray every where, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting." Lot sees the answer before he hears it. Here's the detail to tell a friend: the saying never says what Lot did next. It stops on the offer. If you will. Nobody is pushed into the fire. Like yesterday's leaking basket, the elder teaches with an action, not an argument.
screen: `HE DOESN'T ADD AN ITEM.` · `FINGERS LIKE TEN LAMPS.` · `A LITTLE, ANSWERED WITH ALL.` · `LIFTING UP HOLY HANDS.` · then, large: `BECOME ALL FLAME.`

segments.voice: Sit up and turn your palms upward on your knees, or lift your hands a little if there's room. Keep them open for the whole sit, as if what you bring isn't a list but all of you. If you pray, this is the posture the letter to Timothy describes.
Become all flame. Abba Joseph's answer to a monk who did everything a little: not one more task, the whole life set alight.
Your line: not a longer list: the whole self, given. Nothing on it thrown out, everything on it lit. See you tomorrow.

screen: `DAY 1611 COUNTS.` → `THE SAINTS IN THEIR OWN WORDS · 10 OF 80.` → `TOMORROW: A HUNTER FINDS ANTONY LAUGHING WITH HIS MONKS. WHY?`

howItsDone: Some Christians pray with hands raised or open, alone or in church, and this saying of Abba Joseph is one that people in the monastic tradition pass on.

fork.setup: your friend volunteers at the food bank every Saturday, and spends most of the shift on her phone. by Abba Joseph's answer, what's missing?
options: more shifts, so it finally adds up to something.
nothing; showing up at all is the whole point.
not more hours: all of her, in the hours she gives.
fork.reveal: Joseph didn't lengthen Lot's list or cut it. he answered 'a little' with 'all': the same shift, with the whole person in it.

trapdoor: what you thought: become all flame means burning yourself out doing more.
what it means: the same prayers and the same peace, with the whole person given, not a longer list.
what a scholar hears: an answer given first with the body, hands raised as 1 Timothy 2:8 pictures prayer, and left as an offer: if you will.
guess: the whole life given to God, not a longer list
a fire Joseph lit to warm the visiting monks
burning out from too many prayers and fasts
recall: visions where the Church grows young
an old bishop's thanks before the fire

chat.says: made my senior spring list: choir, youth group, wed supper, bible app streak. what else should i add??
options: Maybe nothing. Joseph didn't add a task; he asked for all of you in what's there.
An early fast or a night of prayer. The longer the list, the more on fire.
Toss the list. Joseph said small things like apps and suppers don't count.
chat.meaning: Joseph threw nothing out and added nothing. He answered Lot's 'a little' with 'all': the same life, wholly given.

tie.story: When Lot asked what more to do, Abba Joseph lifted his hands, his fingers like ten lamps, and said he could become all flame.
tie.friend: Grace doesn't need one more thing on her spring list; she can bring all of herself to the choir, youth group and supper already there.
tie.you: Where could you bring all of you, instead of more?

Abba.meaning: father: a title for a respected desert elder

Lot.meaning: a monk who brings his question to Abba Joseph

Timothy.meaning: the young church leader two New Testament letters are addressed to
